audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on four of seven rows: content win[3..6] all say Akshan while full phases[3].side/[4].side say Skill and [5].side/[6].side say Vladimir. The packet also flags the chart against a 47.19% win rate.
audit.why: A paying reader gets two different answers to 'who wins level 6'. The full layer is the defensible read — Akshan owns 1-3, it evens at 4-6, Vladimir takes over from his first item.
audit.corrected: win[3]=Skill, win[4]=Skill, win[5]=Vladimir, win[6]=Vladimir, matching the existing full-layer sides. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike and phase text claimed Akshan 'stuns' Vladimir, called Hemoplague a map-wide/global-enabling ultimate, and described Sanguine Pool as an invulnerability window his burst can kill through.
audit.why: Akshan has no stun anywhere in his kit. Hemoplague is 625 range, cast on a fight Vladimir is already in. Sanguine Pool is untargetable for 2 seconds — damage does not carry through, so no burst 'kills him through it'.
audit.corrected: Spikes rebuilt around Heroic Swing at level 3 vs a 28-second rank-1 Sanguine Pool, level 6 timing after the pool, first item and anti-heal, and the late tank-that-heals problem.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere stated the interaction that decides this lane: Vladimir heals through chip from Transfusion and Hemoplague, so Grievous Wounds timing is the whole extended-trade question. Hemoplague's per-champion heal was never mentioned.
audit.why: Transfusion costs 0 mana and heals on a 9s-to-4.6s cooldown; Hemoplague heals Vladimir for each champion hit. Akshan's damage pattern is chip-then-execute, which is exactly what that sustain answers.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds early; against Hemoplague it turns a heal-and-amp into just an amp.

audit.whatIsWrong: The pool cooldown was tracked everywhere but never numbered.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16 — 28 seconds at rank 1 is an enormous lane-phase window and makes the advice concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: Late-game text said to burst him before 'passive health regen' kicks in.
audit.why: Crimson Pact is an AP-to-health and health-to-AP conversion, not regeneration. The late problem is that he is a tank with a heal, not that he regenerates.
audit.corrected: Late text now names Crimson Pact and the conversion.

edits.before: Vladimir has no engage before he pools, so once your E is online you can dash in and stun him during his Transfusion cast animation before he can safely Sanguine Pool away.
edits.after: Vladimir has no engage, so once Heroic Swing is online you can land a three-hit string on his Transfusion step-up — Sanguine Pool is 28 seconds at rank 1, so he only escapes one of them.

edits.before: Comeuppance lets you punish his Hemoplague setup — if he ults to enable a dive elsewhere on the map, you can R in fast and either save the ally or catch him before he pools out.
edits.after: Hemoplague is a 625-range zone, not a map tool — he casts it on the fight he is in. Comeuppance punishes the wind-down, but the two seconds of Sanguine Pool eat the release — fire after it.

edits.before: Vladimir's early power is health-pool reliant, and once you have lethality your burst threatens to kill him through Sanguine Pool's brief invulnerability window if you time the follow-up right.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable for two seconds, not invulnerable — your damage does not carry through it. Buy Grievous Wounds early instead; his Transfusion is free and on a 4.6-second cooldown maxed.

edits.before: Vladimir scales into one of the best sustain mages in the game, so you need to end fights fast — camo picks and burst combos before his health regen and pool sustain let him stabilize are your best tool.
edits.after: Vladimir scales into one of the best sustain mages in the game, so end fights fast — Hemoplague heals him per champion it hits, so anti-heal and a camo pick on him alone beat any drawn-out teamfight.

edits.before: Vladimir is entirely reliant on Transfusion poke and has zero mobility besides Sanguine Pool, giving you a wide window to punish once E is unlocked at level 3 — dash in during his cast animation or right after he pools to catch him on cooldown. Early levels 1-2 favor you already since his damage output is low until he stacks health, so aggressive trading pays off from the start.
edits.after: Vladimir is reliant on Transfusion poke and has no mobility besides Sanguine Pool, which is 28 seconds at rank 1 — that is the number the lane runs on. Once Heroic Swing is up at level 3, punish the moment the pool ends, not while he is in it. Levels 1-2 are already yours: his damage is low until he stacks health, so trade on every wave contact.

edits.before: Hemoplague is more of a teamfight/dive enabler than a direct threat to you 1v1, and Comeuppance answers it well if he tries to use it to set up a kill elsewhere on the map. Keep tracking his pool cooldown — that's his only defensive tool, and once it's down he's fully exposed to your combo.
edits.after: Hemoplague is a 625-range zone he drops on a fight he is already in, and it heals him for every champion it hits — Grievous Wounds turns it into a damage amp with no payoff. Keep counting the pool: it is his only defensive tool, and once it is down he is fully exposed.

edits.before: Vladimir becomes very tanky and sustain-heavy with a full build, so your best window to kill him is still early in any skirmish before his passive health regen and pool sustain kick in. Burst him down fast with camouflage engages rather than trying to out-damage him in an extended trade.
edits.after: Crimson Pact converts every point of AP into health, so a full-build Vladimir is a tank you cannot chip down — your window is the opening seconds of a skirmish, before the pool and Hemoplague heal him back. Open with a camouflage flank and anti-heal, never an extended trade.

notes: Level chart was split across layers on four rows (content said Akshan 7/7, full said Skill/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir on rows 3-6). Fixed by moving the content layer onto the full layer's sides as one atomic group, which also resolves the packet defect against the 47.19% win rate. Removed a fabricated Akshan stun, the claim that Hemoplague is global, and the claim that burst kills through Sanguine Pool (it is untargetability, not invulnerability). breakdown.mid, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave, ahead, tldr, tradeGood and tradeBad remain structurally templated — they are shared boilerplate across Akshan's mid matchups — but I had nothing Vladimir-specific left to ground them in after the above without repeating the anti-heal point, so they are left alone rather than reworded.
